correctness.rationale: Using the ordinary disconnected-triple definition, the Alexander dual is exactly the complex of subsets with at most one nonneighbor per vertex. Published shellability gives β=1+n(n−4p−1)/2 and concentration at n−4; equivariant Alexander duality supplies permutation sign. For rotations of order ≥3, an orbit provides two nonneighbors beyond p (including m=4); the half-turn fixes only antipodal edges, each contributing +1 to the Lefschetz count. Formula and rational induced decomposition follow. Independently constructed dual faces for n=9,10,11 p=2 give β=1,6,12 and half-turn trace -4 for n=10. All parameter and orientation edge cases checked.
residual_risks: Uses published nonequivariant shellability theorem, not a new independent proof of its long shelling argument.
Does not classify dihedral/integral structure or n below threshold.
